subproblem.title: Truncated cone map: a Lipschitz H on ℝ^{n+1} that equals (s, u) ↦ s·G(u) near {0 < s < 1, ‖G(u)‖ < ρ}, with its derivative there
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0 (NNReal), ρ ∈ ℝ, and let G : ℝ^n → ℝ^P (Euclid n → Euclid P) be L-Lipschitz. For z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} write z_0 := WithLp.ofLp z 0 and tail z := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) ∈ ℝ^n. Then there is a map H : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P, Lipschitz with some constant K ≥ 0, such that for every z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} with z_0 ∈ (0, 1) and ‖G(tail z)‖ < ρ: (a) H(z) = z_0·G(tail z); and (b) if G is differentiable at tail z, then the tuple (b ↦ DH(z)ê_b) of directional derivatives equals Fin.cons (G(tail z)) (a ↦ z_0·DG(tail z)e_a), i.e. DH(z)ê_0 = G(tail z) and DH(z)ê_{a+1} = z_0·DG(tail z)e_a for a ∈ Fin n. Here D = fderiv ℝ, ê_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (G : Euclid n → Euclid P) (L : NNReal) (ρ : ℝ), LipschitzWith L G → ∃ H : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P, (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K H) ∧ ∀ z : Euclid (n + 1), WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → ‖G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))‖ < ρ → H z = WithLp.ofLp z 0 • G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) ∧ (DifferentiableAt ℝ G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) → (fun b => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single b 1)) = Fin.cons (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))) (fun a => WithLp.ofLp z 0 • fderiv ℝ G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 1, 2, 3(a) and 4 of the selected parent proof (the cone parametrization H_i(s, u) = s·G_i(u)), stated for one Lipschitz map G and an arbitrary radius ρ. This parametrizes Simon's cone 0 ⨯ T = h_#([[(0,1)]] × T), h(t, x) = tx (Ch. 6, 2.30, chapter-06.txt lines 525–536).
Notation. π₀ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ, π₀(z) := z_0 (EuclideanSpace.proj 0), and π′ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^n, π′(z) := tail z. π′ is linear (additivity and homogeneity hold definitionally), so both are continuous linear maps (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap on the finite-dimensional ℝ^{n+1}) and hence Lipschitz with constants ‖π₀‖ and ‖π′‖. On the standard basis: π₀ê_0 = 1, π′ê_0 = 0, π₀ê_{a+1} = 0 and π′ê_{a+1} = e_a. This follows by comparing coordinates: (ê_b)_j = [j = b], Fin.tail shifts indices by Fin.succ, Fin.succ is injective and Fin.succ a ≠ 0.

1. (Radius.) Put ρ′ := max(ρ, 1). Then ρ′ > 0 and ρ′ ≥ ρ.
2. (Retraction.) Let φ be the ContDiffBump centered at 0 ∈ ℝ^P with rIn = ρ′ and rOut = ρ′ + 1 (valid since 0 < ρ′ < ρ′ + 1), and r(y) := φ(y)·y.
 (a) r is C¹, as the product of the smooth φ and the identity, and has compact support because φ does (HasCompactSupport.smul_right). Hence r is Lipschitz with some constant K_r (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport).
 (b) ‖r(y)‖ ≤ ρ′ + 1 for all y. If ‖y‖ < ρ′ + 1, then ‖r(y)‖ = |φ(y)|·‖y‖ ≤ 1·(ρ′ + 1) since 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1. Otherwise dist(y, 0) ≥ rOut, so φ(y) = 0 (ContDiffBump.zero_of_le_dist) and r(y) = 0.
 (c) r(y) = y whenever ‖y‖ ≤ ρ′, because φ = 1 on closedBall(0, rIn) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall).
3. (Clamp.) σ(s) := max(0, min(s, 1)). σ is 1-Lipschitz (s ↦ min(s, 1) and t ↦ max(0, t) are 1-Lipschitz), 0 ≤ σ ≤ 1 so |σ(s)| ≤ 1, and σ(s) = s for s ∈ (0, 1).
4. (Definition.) H(z) := σ(z_0)·r(G(tail z)).
5. (H is Lipschitz.) Put f₁(z) := σ(π₀z) and f₂(z) := r(G(π′z)). f₁ is ‖π₀‖-Lipschitz with |f₁| ≤ 1, and f₂ is K_r·L·‖π′‖-Lipschitz with ‖f₂‖ ≤ ρ′ + 1 (steps 2 and 3). For z, z′ ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, H(z) − H(z′) = (f₁(z) − f₁(z′))·f₂(z) + f₁(z′)·(f₂(z) − f₂(z′)). Hence
 ‖H(z) − H(z′)‖ ≤ |f₁(z) − f₁(z′)|·‖f₂(z)‖ + |f₁(z′)|·‖f₂(z) − f₂(z′)‖ ≤ ((ρ′ + 1)·‖π₀‖ + K_r·L·‖π′‖)·‖z − z′‖,
 so H is Lipschitz with constant K := ((ρ′ + 1)‖π₀‖ + K_r L ‖π′‖)₊ (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le').
6. (Local form; part (a).) Fix z with z_0 ∈ (0, 1) and ‖G(tail z)‖ < ρ. Let H̃(z′) := π₀(z′)·G(π′z′) and O := {z′ : π₀z′ ∈ (0, 1), ‖G(π′z′)‖ < ρ′}. O is open, as the intersection of the preimages of the open sets (0, 1) and (−∞, ρ′) under continuous maps (G is continuous because it is Lipschitz). z ∈ O because ‖G(tail z)‖ < ρ ≤ ρ′. For z′ ∈ O, σ(z′_0) = z′_0 by step 3 and r(G(tail z′)) = G(tail z′) by step 2(c), since ‖G(tail z′)‖ < ρ′. So H = H̃ on the neighbourhood O of z, i.e. H =ᶠ[𝓝 z] H̃. In particular H(z) = z_0·G(tail z), which is (a).
7. (Derivative.) Assume G is differentiable at u := tail z. π₀ and π′ are continuous linear, so G∘π′ has derivative DG(u)∘π′ at z (chain rule). By the product rule (HasFDerivAt.smul), H̃ has at z the derivative D := z_0·(DG(u)∘π′) + π₀.smulRight(G(u)), that is D(v) = z_0·DG(u)(π′v) + (π₀v)·G(u). Since H =ᶠ[𝓝 z] H̃, DH(z) = DH̃(z) = D (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, HasFDerivAt.fderiv).
8. (Evaluation on the basis; part (b).) From π₀ê_0 = 1 and π′ê_0 = 0 we get D(ê_0) = z_0·DG(u)(0) + 1·G(u) = G(u). From π₀ê_{a+1} = 0 and π′ê_{a+1} = e_a we get D(ê_{a+1}) = z_0·DG(u)e_a. By Fin.cases on b ∈ Fin (n+1) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ), the tuple (b ↦ DH(z)ê_b) equals Fin.cons (G(u)) (a ↦ z_0·DG(u)e_a), which is (b). ∎

proof_key_steps: ρ′ := max(ρ, 1). Let r(y) := φ(y)·y, with φ the ContDiffBump with radii ρ′ < ρ′ + 1. Then r is Lipschitz (C¹ with compact support), ‖r‖ ≤ ρ′ + 1 and r = id on closedBall(0, ρ′). The clamp σ(s) := max(0, min(s, 1)) is 1-Lipschitz, |σ| ≤ 1 and σ = id on (0, 1).
H(z) := σ(z_0)·r(G(tail z)) is Lipschitz, by the product estimate using the bounds on σ and r and the Lipschitz coordinate maps.
On the open set O = {z′ : z′_0 ∈ (0, 1), ‖G(tail z′)‖ < ρ′} ∋ z, H coincides with H̃(z′) := z′_0·G(tail z′), so H(z) = z_0·G(tail z).
By the product and chain rules and EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, DH(z)v = z_0·DG(u)(tail v) + v_0·G(u). Evaluating at ê_0 and ê_{a+1} gives Fin.cons (G(u)) (a ↦ z_0·DG(u)e_a).

subproblem.title: Cone piece change of variables: ∫_A w·η(G)(DG e) = ∫_B (w∘tail)·ω(H)(DH ê) when η = Kω on G(A) and H(s, u) = s·G(u) on B
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0 (NNReal), G : ℝ^n → ℝ^P any map, H : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P L-Lipschitz, A ⊆ ℝ^n Borel, and w : ℝ^n → ℤ measurable with (w : ℝ) Lebesgue integrable on A. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P) be a test form (TestFormOn univ (n+1): a smooth (n+1)-form with compact support) and let η be any n-form on ℝ^P (a map ℝ^P → Λ^n). Write z_0 := WithLp.ofLp z 0, tail z := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)), and B := {z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} : z_0 ∈ (0, 1) and tail z ∈ A}. Assume:
(H1) for every z ∈ B, H(z) = z_0·G(tail z) and the tuple (b ↦ DH(z)ê_b) equals Fin.cons (G(tail z)) (a ↦ z_0·DG(tail z)e_a);
(H2) for every u ∈ A, η(G u) = ∫_0^1 t^n·(ω(t·G u)).curryLeft (G u) dt, an interval integral of n-covectors; this is Kω(G u) for the radial homotopy operator K.
Then ∫_{u ∈ A} w(u)·η(G u)(DG(u)e_0, …, DG(u)e_{n−1}) du = ∫_{z ∈ B} w(tail z)·ω(H z)(DH(z)ê_0, …, DH(z)ê_n) dz. Here D = fderiv ℝ, e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^n, ê_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, and all measures are Lebesgue measure.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (G : Euclid n → Euclid P) (H : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (w : Euclid n → ℤ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)) (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n), LipschitzWith L H → MeasurableSet A → Measurable w → IntegrableOn (fun u => (w u : ℝ)) A → (∀ z : Euclid (n + 1), WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A → H z = WithLp.ofLp z 0 • G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) ∧ (fun b => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single b 1)) = Fin.cons (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))) (fun a => WithLp.ofLp z 0 • fderiv ℝ G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) → (∀ u ∈ A, η (G u) = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ n • ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (n + 1)) (t • G u)).curryLeft (G u)) → ∫ u in A, (w u : ℝ) * η (G u) (fun a => fderiv ℝ G u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1)) = ∫ z in {z : Euclid (n + 1) | WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A}, (w (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) : ℝ) * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (n + 1)) (H z) (fun b => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single b 1))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 8(a)–(c) of the selected parent proof, for one piece. It is the parametrized form of the cone formula behind Simon Ch. 6, 2.30 (chapter-06.txt lines 525–536). With h(t, x) = tx, the computation in the proof of 2.27 (lines 468–476) reads h_#([[(0,1)]] × T)(ω) = ∫_0^1 ∫ ⟨ω(tx), x ∧ t^n T⃗(x)⟩ dμ_T(x) dt. Uses the siblings cyl_fubini (the accepted cmcdt_lpi_cyl_fubini) and pullback_integrable (the accepted cmcdt_lpi_cyl_pullback_integrable).
Notation. ι(t, u) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp u)) ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, so that ι(t, u)_0 = t and tail ι(t, u) = u. DG(u)e := (a ↦ DG(u)e_a) and DH(z)ê := (b ↦ DH(z)ê_b). h(z) := w(tail z), and F(z) := h(z)·ω(H z)(DH(z)ê).

1. (h is integrable on B.) h is measurable (w is measurable as a map out of ℤ, and tail is continuous). By cyl_fubini (b) with f = ‖h‖ₑ, ∫⁻_B ‖h‖ₑ = ∫⁻_A ∫⁻_{(0,1)} ‖w(u)‖ₑ dt du = ∫⁻_A ‖w(u)‖ₑ du < ∞, using vol((0, 1)) = 1 and the integrability of w on A. So h is integrable on B.
2. (F is integrable on B.) Apply pullback_integrable with Q := P, n := n+1, the L-Lipschitz map H, S := B, g := h and the test form ω. It shows that z ↦ h(z)·ω(H z)(DH(z)ê), which is F, is integrable on B.
3. (Fubini.) By step 2 and cyl_fubini (c), ∫_B F = ∫_{u ∈ A} ∫_{t ∈ (0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt du. Since A is measurable, it suffices (setIntegral_congr_fun) to prove for every u ∈ A that
 w(u)·η(G u)(DG(u)e) = ∫_{(0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt.   (†)
 Fix u ∈ A and write v := G(u) and x := DG(u)e ∈ (ℝ^P)^n.
4. (Inner integrand.) Let t ∈ (0, 1) and z := ι(t, u). Then z_0 = t ∈ (0, 1) and tail z = u ∈ A, so z ∈ B. By (H1), H(z) = t·v and DH(z)ê = Fin.cons v (a ↦ t·x_a). For every (n+1)-covector α, α(Fin.cons v (a ↦ t·x_a)) = (α.curryLeft v)(a ↦ t·x_a) = t^n·(α.curryLeft v)(x) = t^n·α(Fin.cons v x). This uses curryLeft_apply_apply, with Matrix.vecCons = Fin.cons, and multilinearity (map_smul_univ, ∏_{a ∈ Fin n} t = t^n). Hence
 F(ι(t, u)) = w(u)·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v (a ↦ t·x_a)) = w(u)·(t^n·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v x)).
 Integrating over (0, 1) (setIntegral_congr_fun on the measurable (0, 1), then integral_const_mul) gives ∫_{(0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt = w(u)·∫_{(0,1)} t^n·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v x) dt.
5. (The homotopy integral.) By (H2), η(v) = ∫_0^1 k(t) dt with k(t) := t^n·(ω(t·v)).curryLeft v. k is continuous. Indeed t ↦ ω(t·v) is continuous (ω is smooth), and β ↦ β.curryLeft v is continuous linear, being β ↦ (curryLeftLI β)(v) for the linear isometry curryLeftLI. So k is interval integrable on [0, 1]. Evaluation at the fixed tuple x, E_x(β) := β(x), is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply). Hence, by ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm,
 η(v)(x) = E_x(∫_0^1 k) = ∫_0^1 E_x(k(t)) dt = ∫_0^1 t^n·((ω(t·v)).curryLeft v)(x) dt = ∫_0^1 t^n·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v x) dt,
 again by curryLeft_apply_apply. Since 0 ≤ 1, the interval integral equals the integral over (0, 1] (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le), which equals the integral over (0, 1) because single points are null (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo).
6. (Conclusion.) Steps 4 and 5 give (†): w(u)·η(G u)(DG(u)e) = w(u)·∫_{(0,1)} t^n·ω(t·v)(Fin.cons v x) dt = ∫_{(0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt. With step 3, ∫_A w(u)·η(G u)(DG(u)e) du = ∫_A ∫_{(0,1)} F(ι(t, u)) dt du = ∫_B F, which is the claim. ∎

subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ) (G : Euclid n → Euclid P) (H : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (w : Euclid n → ℤ) (c : Euclid n → ℝ), Measurable G → MeasurableSet A → Measurable w → Measurable c → IntegrableOn (fun u => (w u : ℝ)) A → (∀ u ∈ A, ‖G u‖ ≤ ρ) → (∀ u ∈ A, 0 ≤ c u ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |α (fun a => fderiv ℝ G u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))| ≤ c u * covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ z : Euclid (n + 1), WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A → (fun b => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single b 1)) = Fin.cons (G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))) (fun a => WithLp.ofLp z 0 • fderiv ℝ G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) → IntegrableOn (fun z : Euclid (n + 1) => (w (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) : ℝ)) {z : Euclid (n + 1) | WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A} ∧ (∀ z : Euclid (n + 1), WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 → (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A → 0 ≤ WithLp.ofLp z 0 ^ n * ‖G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))‖ * c (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1), |α (fun b => fderiv ℝ H z (EuclideanSpace.single b 1))| ≤ WithLp.ofLp z 0 ^ n * ‖G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))‖ * c (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ ∫⁻ z in {z : Euclid (n + 1) | WithLp.ofLp z 0 ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)) : Euclid n) ∈ A}, ENNReal.ofReal (|(w (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))) : ℝ)| * (WithLp.ofLp z 0 ^ n * ‖G (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z)))‖ * c (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp z))))) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ρ * ∫⁻ u in A, ENNReal.ofReal (|(w u : ℝ)| * c u)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 3(c), 5, 6 and 7 of the selected parent proof, for one piece. Uses the siblings cyl_fubini (the accepted cmcdt_lpi_cyl_fubini) and curry_le (the accepted cmcdt_lp_covector_curryLeft_norm_le).
Notation. ι(t, u) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp u)) ∈ ℝ^{n+1} for t ∈ ℝ, u ∈ ℝ^n. Then ι(t, u)_0 = t and tail ι(t, u) = u (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, WithLp.ofLp_toLp). For an n-covector β, βDG(u)e denotes β(a ↦ DG(u)e_a).

0. (Preliminaries.) z ↦ z_0 and z ↦ tail z are continuous, hence measurable. u ↦ (w(u) : ℝ) is measurable, since every map out of the countable discrete ℤ is measurable (measurable_of_countable). By cyl_fubini applied to (n, A), B is measurable, and for every measurable f : ℝ^{n+1} → [0, ∞]
 ∫⁻_B f = ∫⁻_{u ∈ A} ∫⁻_{t ∈ (0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du.   (∗)
1. (Part (i).) h := w∘tail is measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable. Apply (∗) to f(z) := ‖h(z)‖ₑ, so that f(ι(t, u)) = ‖w(u)‖ₑ: ∫⁻_B ‖h‖ₑ = ∫⁻_A ∫⁻_{(0,1)} ‖w(u)‖ₑ dt du = ∫⁻_A ‖w(u)‖ₑ·vol((0, 1)) du = ∫⁻_A ‖w(u)‖ₑ du < ∞. Here vol((0, 1)) = 1 (Real.volume_Ioo), and the last integral is finite because w is integrable on A. So h is integrable on B.
2. (Covector identity.) For an (n+1)-covector α, x ∈ ℝ^P, v ∈ (ℝ^P)^n and s ∈ ℝ:
 α(Fin.cons x (a ↦ s·v_a)) = (α.curryLeft x)(a ↦ s·v_a) = (∏_{a ∈ Fin n} s)·(α.curryLeft x)(v) = s^n·(α.curryLeft x)(v).
 The first equality is ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply (α.curryLeft x v = α(Matrix.vecCons x v), and Matrix.vecCons = Fin.cons definitionally). The second is multilinearity (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ).
3. (Part (ii).) Fix z ∈ B and put s := z_0 ∈ (0, 1), u := tail z ∈ A and v := G(u). Then c′(z) = s^n·‖v‖·c(u) ≥ 0, because s > 0, ‖v‖ ≥ 0 and c(u) ≥ 0. Let α be an (n+1)-covector. By the hypothesis on DH at z ∈ B and step 2,
 α(DH(z)ê) = α(Fin.cons v (a ↦ s·DG(u)e_a)) = s^n·(α.curryLeft v)(DG(u)e).
 Hence, using s^n ≥ 0, then the hypothesis on c at u applied to the n-covector α.curryLeft v, then curry_le (|α.curryLeft v| ≤ ‖v‖·|α|) together with c(u) ≥ 0:
 |α(DH(z)ê)| = s^n·|(α.curryLeft v)(DG(u)e)| ≤ s^n·c(u)·|α.curryLeft v| ≤ s^n·c(u)·‖v‖·|α| = c′(z)·|α|.
4. (Part (iii).) The function f(z) := ofReal(|w(tail z)|·c′(z)) is measurable, as a composition of products of measurable functions (G and c are measurable). By (∗),
 ∫⁻_B f = ∫⁻_{u ∈ A} ∫⁻_{t ∈ (0,1)} ofReal(|w(u)|·(t^n·‖G(u)‖·c(u))) dt du.
 Fix u ∈ A. Then c(u) ≥ 0 and 0 ≤ ‖G(u)‖ ≤ ρ, so in particular ρ ≥ 0. For t ∈ (0, 1) we have 0 ≤ t^n ≤ 1, hence |w(u)|·(t^n·‖G(u)‖·c(u)) ≤ |w(u)|·(1·ρ·c(u)) = ρ·(|w(u)|·c(u)), and ofReal(ρ·x) = ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(x) because ρ ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). Therefore the inner integral is at most ∫⁻_{(0,1)} ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u)) dt = ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u))·vol((0, 1)) = ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u)) (setLIntegral_mono, setLIntegral_const).
 Integrating over A (setLIntegral_mono, the right side being measurable) and pulling out the constant (lintegral_const_mul) gives
 ∫⁻_B f ≤ ∫⁻_A ofReal(ρ)·ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u)) du = ofReal(ρ)·∫⁻_A ofReal(|w(u)|·c(u)) du.
 (If A = ∅ both sides vanish; the inequality ρ ≥ 0 is only used at points u ∈ A.) ∎

proof_key_steps: cyl_fubini: B is Borel and ∫⁻_B f = ∫⁻_A ∫⁻_{(0,1)} f(ι(t, u)) dt du. With f = ‖w∘tail‖ₑ this gives ∫⁻_B |w∘tail| = ∫⁻_A |w| < ∞, so w∘tail is integrable on B.
α(Fin.cons v (a ↦ s·x_a)) = s^n·(α.curryLeft v)(x), by curryLeft_apply_apply and map_smul_univ.
For z ∈ B, with s = z_0 and u = tail z: |α(DH(z)ê)| = s^n·|(α.curryLeft (G u))(DG(u)e)| ≤ s^n·c(u)·|α.curryLeft (G u)| ≤ s^n·c(u)·‖G u‖·|α| = c′(z)·|α|, by the c-bound and then curry_le.
Tonelli via cyl_fubini, with t^n ≤ 1, ‖G u‖ ≤ ρ and vol((0, 1)) = 1, gives ∫⁻_B |w∘tail|·c′ ≤ ofReal(ρ)·∫⁻_A |w|·c.

Tonelli proves weight integrability; multilinearity and curry_le prove the coefficient bound; the radius bound and t^n ≤ 1 prove the ENNReal mass estimate. Positivity is justified locally, including the empty-set case. Both declared dependencies are used correctly.
